The '''2025–26 season''' was [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|122nd season in existence]] and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|95th consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2025–26 La Liga|domestic league]], Real Madrid participated in this season's editions of the [[2025–26 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2026 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

This season was the first since [[2011–12 Real Madrid CF season|2011–12]] without [[Luka Modrić]], as well as the first since [[2014–15 Real Madrid CF season|2014–15]] without youth graduate [[Lucas Vázquez]], who both departed as free agents, to [[AC Milan]] and [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], respectively.<ref name=":0"/><ref name=":2"/>

==Summary==
===Pre-season===
On 17 May 2025, during the [[2024–25 Real Madrid CF season|2024–25]] season, Madrid announced the signing of [[Dean Huijsen]] from [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], with the Spanish center-back joining the club on 1 June and signing a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Huijsen, new Real Madrid player|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/huijsen-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-17-05-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=17 May 2025|access-date=17 May 2025|archive-date=17 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250517103136/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/huijsen-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-17-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On 22 May, Madrid announced the departure of the club captain [[Luka Modrić]] after 13 years in the club, who left as Real's most decorated player, having won 28 trophies.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cortegana|first1=Mario|last2=Rai|first2=Guillermo|title=Luka Modrić announces Real Madrid departure|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6235469/2025/05/22/luka-modric-real-madrid-leaves|publisher=The Athletic|date=22 May 2025|access-date=22 May 2025|archive-date=22 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522170905/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6235469/2025/05/22/luka-modric-real-madrid-leaves/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 May, Madrid and [[Carlo Ancelotti]] announced their mutual decision to part ways after the conclusion of the [[2024–25 La Liga|2024–25 La Liga campaign]], with the Italian coach leaving as the [[List of Real Madrid CF managers#Trophies|most decorated]] manager in the history of the club with 15 trophies.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Ancelotti|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-ancelotti-23-05-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=23 May 2025|access-date=24 May 2025|archive-date=24 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250524081755/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-ancelotti-23-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 May, Madrid announced the appointment of [[Xabi Alonso]] as their new manager for the next three seasons, starting from 1 June.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Xabi Alonso|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=25 May 2025|access-date=25 May 2025|archive-date=25 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525103017/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 May, Madrid and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] announced an agreement for the transfer of [[Trent Alexander-Arnold]], with the Englishman joining the club on 1 June on a six-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexander-Arnold signs for Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/perfil-arnold-30-05-2025|date=30 May 2025|access-date=30 May 2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=30 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530104914/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/perfil-arnold-30-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On the same day, the club announced the departure of [[Jesús Vallejo]] upon the expiration of his contract.<ref name=:1>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Jesús Vallejo|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-jesus-vallejo-30-05-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=30 May 2025|access-date=30 May 2025|archive-date=30 May Madrid announced that [[Franco Mastantuono]] would join the club from [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] on 14 August, penning a six-year deal with the player.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mastantuono signs for Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/mastantuono-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-13-06-2025|date=13 June 2025|access-date=13 June 2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=13 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250613133404/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/mastantuono-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-13-06-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 July, Madrid brought back their [[Real Madrid Castilla|youth academy]] product [[Álvaro Carreras]], signing him from [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] on a six-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Álvaro Carreras joins Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/alvaro-carreras-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-14-07-2025|date=14 July 2025|access-date=14 July 2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=14 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714182326/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/alvaro-carreras-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-14-07-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, Madrid announced the departure of [[Lucas Vázquez]], who spent 10 seasons at the club and won 23 trophies.<ref name=":2"/> On 8 August, Madrid extended [[Gonzalo García (footballer, born 2004)|Gonzalo García]]'s contract until 2030 and promoted him to the first team from [[Real Madrid Castilla|Castilla]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Gonzalo García has signed new Real Madrid contract after breakthrough Club World Cup|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6510526/2025/08/08/gonzalo-garcia-real-madrid-contract|publisher=The Athletic|date=8 August 2025|access-date=8 August 2025|archive-date=8 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250808195710/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6510526/2025/08/08/gonzalo-garcia-real-madrid-contract/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===August===
Madrid started their La Liga campaign on 19 August with a 1–0 home win over [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], thanks to a converted penalty from [[Kylian Mbappé]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Stynes|first=Trevor|title=Mbappé penalty earns Real Madrid 1–0 win over stubborn Osasuna|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/mbappe-penalty-earns-real-1-0-win-over-stubborn-osasuna-2025-08-19/|website=Reuters|publisher=Thomson Reuters|date=19 August 2025|access-date=20 August 2025|archive-date=24 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824145423/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/mbappe-penalty-earns-real-1-0-win-over-stubborn-osasuna-2025-08-19/|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Madrid faced newly-promoted [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]] away from home, winning 3–0 with a brace from Mbappé and [[Vinícius Júnior]]'s goal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lund|first=Tommy|title=Real Madrid too strong for Oviedo as Mbappé and Vinícius strike|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/real-madrid-too-strong-oviedo-mbappe-vinicius-strike-2025-08-24/|website=Reuters|publisher=Thomson Reuters|date=24 August 2025|access-date=24 August 2025|archive-date=25 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250825112417/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/real-madrid-too-strong-oviedo-mbappe-vinicius-strike-2025-08-24/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 August, goals from [[Arda Güler]] and Vinícius helped Madrid to come from behind and get a 2–1 victory over [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] at the [[Bernabéu (stadium)|Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Mallorca: Xabi Alonso's side come from behind to seal third win of La Liga season|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp89733jnl2t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=30 August 2025|access-date=31 August 2025|archive-date=31 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250831090014/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp89733jnl2t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===September===
On 13 September, the first match on the month ended in a ten-man 2–1 win over [[Real Sociedad]] at the [[Anoeta Stadium]], as Mbappé and Güler got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Abraham|first=Timothy|title=Real Sociedad 1–2 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé scores one and sets up another|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/czdj4y16ql6t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=13 September 2025|access-date=13 September 2025|archive-date=13 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250913175755/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/czdj4y16ql6t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Mbappé's brace from the penalty spot rescued three points for the team, as ten-man Madrid beat [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] 2–1 in the opening matchday of the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League league phase|Champions League league phase]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Salley|first=Emily|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Marseille: Kylian Mbappé scores two penalties as 10-man hosts fight back|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjw72dnl36dt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=16 September 2025|access-date=17 September 2025|archive-date=17 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250917074733/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjw72dnl36dt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 20 September, Madrid continued their winning streak with a 2–0 victory against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], with [[Éder Militão]] and Mbappé scoring for the team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Millington|first=Adam|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Espanyol: Kylian Mbappé scores again as Real continue winning run|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpw17y5rg71t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=20 September 2025|access-date=20 September 2025|archive-date=20 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250920173741/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpw17y5rg71t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, goals from Vinícius and Mastantuono, a debut one for the Argentinian, and Mbappé's brace helped Madrid to a 4–1 win at [[Levante UD|Levante]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Abraham|first=Timothy|title=Levante 1–4 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé scores twice as Xabi Alonso's side notch up their sixth consecutive win in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4g90w32pe2t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=23 September 2025|access-date=23 September 2025|archive-date=23 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250923220432/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4g90w32pe2t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 27 September, Madrid suffered their first defeat of the season in a 2–5 loss to [[Atlético Madrid]] with goals from Mbappé and Güler, conceding five to [[Madrid derby]] rivals for the first time since [[1950–51 Real Madrid CF season|1950]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Oscroft|first=Tim|title=Atlético Madrid 5–2 Real Madrid: Xabi Alonso's side concede five in derby|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0q7ppe8wq8t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=27 September 2025|access-date=27 September 2025|archive-date=27 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250927204255/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0q7ppe8wq8t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, courtesy of a hat-trick from Mbappé and goals from [[Eduardo Camavinga]] and [[Brahim Díaz]], ''Los Blancos'' beat their Champions League opponents [[FC Kairat|Kairat]] 5–0.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Kairat 0–5 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé reaches 60 Champions League goals|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce3ye4vz3w1t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=30 September 2025|access-date=30 September 2025|archive-date=30 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930190534/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce3ye4vz3w1t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===October===
On 4 October, Vinícius' brace combined with a goal from Mbappé gave Madrid a 3–1 league win over [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] at the Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Villarreal: Vinícius Junior scores twice as Real go top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/czewx8ej69pt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 October 2025|access-date=4 Real Madrid: Real go top of La Liga as protests continue|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cqjwr771p71t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=19 October 2025|access-date=20 October scores first goal of season in Real win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr43rxk47qwt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=22 October 2025|access-date=23 October 2025|archive-date=23 October Madrid pull clear of Barcelona|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/26/real-madrid-barcelona-el-clasico-la-liga-match-report|publisher=The Guardian|date=26 October 2025|access-date=26 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251026180531/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/26/real-madrid-barcelona-el-clasico-la-liga-match-report|url-status=live}}</ref>

===November===
Madrid started the month on 1 November, trashing [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] 4–0, as a brace from Mbappé and goals from Bellingham and Carreras, a debut one for the Spaniard, helped Real to take the win.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rajan|first=Adwaidh|title=Real Madrid 4–0 Valencia: Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham score as hosts extend La Liga against Liverpool 0–1 away from home.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Liverpool 1–0 Real Madrid: Alexis Mac Allister scores with Reds back to their best to beat in a 0–0 stalemate.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid held by Rayo Vallecano in drab draw|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0l7xx1kjwzt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=9 November Returning from another international break on 23 November, the debut goal from Huijsen and a tap-in from Bellingham rescued one point for Madrid in a 2–2 draw at [[Elche CF|Elche]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Elche 2–2 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham shines as visitors go top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c7v82yep4z4t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=23 November 2025|access-date=23 November 2025|archive-date=23 November 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251123221727/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c7v82yep4z4t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Mbappé scored four goals to seal a 4–3 Champions League win over [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] for Real.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Olympiacos 3–4 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé scores four in Real win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c773lzd40j6t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 November 2025|access-date=27 November 2025|archive-date=28 November 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251128100706/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c773lzd40j6t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 November, Madrid dropped points in La Liga for the third time in a row, drawing 1–1 away against Girona with a goal from Mbappé.<ref>{{cite web|last=Millington|first=Adam|title=Mbappé penalty earns Real Madrid draw at Girona|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgl64799xr3t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=30 November 2025|access-date=1 December 2025|archive-date=1 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251201082041/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgl64799xr3t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===December===
First match of the month ended with a 3–0 away win at [[Athletic Bilbao]] on 3 December, ending Madrid's three-match league winless streak, as Mbappé got on the scoresheet twice, as well as Camavinga.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Athletic Club 0–3 Real Madrid: Trent Alexander-Arnold injured as visitors cruise to win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c79xdrlq5w9t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=3 December 2025|access-date=4 December 2025|archive-date=3 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251203205454/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c79xdrlq5w9t|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] handed Madrid a 0–2 defeat at the Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Madrid stunned by Celta Vigo as they have two sent off|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5y9l1r2pn9t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=7 December 2025|access-date=8 December 2025|archive-date=8 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208210320/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5y9l1r2pn9t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 December, Madrid faced [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at home in the Champions League, but were unable to earn any points, losing 1–2 with a goal from [[Rodrygo]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Hamez|first=Shamoon|title=Real Madrid 1–2 Man City: Rodrygo, O'Reilly and Haaland score|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clyk8x8nr41t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=10 December 2025|access-date=11 December 2025|archive-date=11 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211071548/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clyk8x8nr41t|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, goals from Mbappé and Rodrygo earned Madrid a 2–1 win at [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Alavés 1–2 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé scores 70th goal for Madrid in much-needed win for under pressure boss Xabi Alonso|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cvgkdewnv95t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 December 2025|access-date=18 December 2025|archive-date=18 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251218171847/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cvgkdewnv95t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 December, Madrid entered [[2025–26 Copa del Rey|this season's Copa del Rey edition]], beating [[CF Talavera de la Reina|Talavera de la Reina]] 3–2 through Mbappé's brace and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|last=MacDonald|first=Keifer|title=Talavera 2–3 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé one short of equalling Cristiano Ronaldo record|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx2ddvxjv7wt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 December 2025|access-date=18 December 2025|archive-date=18 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251218171846/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx2ddvxjv7wt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid closed the year on a high, getting a 2–0 win over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], courtesy of goals from Bellingham and Mbappé.<ref>{{cite web|last=Abraham|first=Timothy|title=Mbappé equals Ronaldo record as Real Madrid beat Sevilla|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwyv8p8l4mmt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=20 December 2025|access-date=20 December 2025|archive-date=20 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251220230808/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwyv8p8l4mmt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 December, Madrid loaned out [[Endrick]] to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Endrick|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-endrick-23-12-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=23 December 2025|access-date=24 December 2025|archive-date=24 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251224145348/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-endrick-23-12-2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

===January===
On 4 January, Madrid started their year, as Gonzalo García's hat-trick and goals from [[Raúl Asencio (footballer, born 2003)|Raúl Asencio]] and [[Fran García (footballer, born 1999)|Fran García]] gave Real a crushing 5–1 victory over [[Real Betis]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Oscroft|first=Tim|title=García grabs hat-trick as Real Madrid thrash Betis|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce8r0m8ml14t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 January 2026|access-date=4 January 2026|archive-date=4 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260104175456/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce8r0m8ml14t|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, goals from Valverde and Rodrygo helped Madrid to get a 2–1 win over city rivals Atlético Madrid and reach the [[2026 Supercopa de España final|Supercopa de España final]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Real Madrid beat Atlético to reach Spanish Super Cup final|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c801l1my7ppt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=8 January 2026|access-date=9 January 2026|archive-date=9 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260109210125/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c801l1my7ppt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 January, goals from Vinícius and Gonzalo García were not enough for success in the Supercopa de España final, as Madrid finished as runners-up with a 2–3 loss against Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|last=Anderson|first=Jess|title=Barcelona 3–2 Real Madrid: Raphinha scores winner as Barcelona triumph in Spanish Super Cup|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c75x71y5rl9t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=11 January 2026|access-date=11 January 2026|archive-date=11 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260111212952/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c75x71y5rl9t|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Madrid and Alonso parted ways by mutual agreement, with [[Álvaro Arbeloa]] being appointed the new head coach.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Xabi Alonso|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-12-01-2026|date=12 January 2026|access-date=12 January 2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=12 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112201030/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-12-01-2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Álvaro Arbeloa|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-alvaro-arbeloa-12-01-2026|date=12 January 2026|access-date=12 January 2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=12 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112201813/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-alvaro-arbeloa-12-01-2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, Arbeloa's first match ended in an disappointing early Copa del Rey exit, as Madrid lost 2–3 to [[Segunda División|second-division]] [[Albacete Balompié|Albacete]] with goals from Mastantuono and Gonzalo García.<ref>{{cite web|last1=MacDonald|first1=Keifer|last2=Conway|first2=Elizabeth|title=Real Madrid stunned by Albacete in Copa del Rey|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy8pe7x2ekvt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 January 2026|access-date=15 January 2026|archive-date=14 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114230308/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy8pe7x2ekvt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 January, Madrid returned to winning ways, beating Levante 2–0 at home, as Mbappé and Asencio got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=MacDonald|first=Keifer|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Levante: Kylian Mbappé scores in Álvaro Arbeloa's first league match|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c62vnjl2krrt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 January 2026|access-date=17 January 2026|archive-date=17 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260117170819/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c62vnjl2krrt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Mbappé's brace and strikes from Mastantuono, Vinícius and Bellingham, as well as an own goal, saw Madrid take a dominating 6–1 win over [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Real Madrid 6–1 Monaco: Kylian Mbappé scores twice against former club in convincing win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cedwvw4nwppt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=20 January 2026|access-date=20 January 2026|archive-date=20 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260120221934/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cedwvw4nwppt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 January, two goals from Mbappé sealed three points for Madrid, as Real won 2–0 against Villarreal at the [[Estadio de la Cerámica|La Cerámica]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Villarreal 0–2 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé double sends Real Madrid top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp8753j20xdt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=24 January 2026|access-date=24 January 2026|archive-date=24 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260124222209/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp8753j20xdt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid suffered a 2–4 defeat against Benfica in the Champions League, with Mbappé scoring both goals for the team, and dropped out of the top eight, having to play in the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Knockout phase play-offs|knockout phase play-offs]] for the second season in a row.<ref>{{cite web|last=Drury|first=Sam|title=Benfica 4–2 Real Madrid: Goalkeeper Anatoliy Trubin's 98th-minute header puts José Mourinho's side into play-offs|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c62rdzw6lzrt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=28 January 2026|access-date=30 January 2026|archive-date=30 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130071725/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c62rdzw6lzrt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, a goal from Vinícius and Mbappé's [[Association football#Duration and tie-breaking methods|injury time]] penalty winner gave Madrid a 2–1 win over Rayo Vallecano.<ref>{{cite web|last=Oscroft|first=Tim|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Rayo Vallecano: Kylian Mbappé scores late penalty after Jude Bellingham injury|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3vpvdenlnt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=1 February 2026|access-date=1 February 2026|archive-date=1 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201161134/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3vpvdenlnt|url-status=live}}</ref> A week later, Madrid beat Valencia 2–0 on the road, as Carreras and Mbappé got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Howarth|first=Matthew|title=Real Madrid beat Valencia to close gap to leaders Barca|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpv7gxw0ry0t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=8 February 2026|access-date=9 February 2026|archive-date=9 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260209083934/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpv7gxw0ry0t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 February, Gonzalo García's goal, a double from Vinícius and a strike from Valverde helped Madrid to a 4–1 victory over Real Sociedad.<ref>{{cite web|last=MacDonald|first=Keifer|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Real Sociedad: Trent Alexander-Arnold get assist on return|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5yvj2qn54jt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 February 2026|access-date=15 February 2026|archive-date=15 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260215185002/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5yvj2qn54jt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, a lone goal from Vinícius sealed a 1–0 win over knockout phase play-offs opponents Benfica in the first leg.<ref>{{cite web|last=Poole|first=Harry|title=Vinícius' brilliant winner beats Benfica in game halted for alleged racism|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c93jq0jqzypt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 February 2026|access-date=19 February 2026|archive-date=19 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260219105238/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c93jq0jqzypt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 21 February, Madrid suffered a 1–2 loss at Osasuna, as Vinícius' goal was not enough for any points.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Osasuna 2–1 Real Madrid: Vinícius Jr scores but Real Madrid beaten by Osasuna|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwy9e763vx5t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=21 February 2026|access-date=22 February 2026|archive-date=22 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260222184149/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwy9e763vx5t|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid played the return leg of the knockout phase play-offs, as goals from [[Aurélien Tchouaméni]] and Vinícius secured a 2–1 victory against Benfica and progression to the round of 16 with a 3–1 win on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rose|first=Gary|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Benfica (3–1 agg): Vinícius Jr scores as Real reach Champions League last 16|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq5747devq8t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=25 February 2026|access-date=26 February 2026|archive-date=25 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260225232535/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq5747devq8t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===March===
On 2 March, Madrid's first game of the month turned out to be their second consecutive league defeat, losing to Getafe 0–1 at home.<ref>{{cite web|last=Booth|first=George|title=Real Madrid 0–1 Getafe: Satriano's spectacular strike hands defeat to Madrid|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5yr5qp0jnpt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=2 March 2026|access-date=6 March 2026|archive-date=2 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260302223404/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5yr5qp0jnpt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, a goal from Tchouaméni, as well as Valverde's late winner, gave Madrid three points in a 2–1 win over Celta Vigo.<ref>{{cite web|title=Celta Vigo 1–2 Real Madrid: Federico Valverde scores late winner to cut Barcelona lead in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgqgzd55nq1t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=6 March 2026|access-date=7 March 2026|archive-date=7 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260307092847/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgqgzd55nq1t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 March, Madrid faced Manchester City, playing the English side for the fifth consecutive Champions League knockout phase, as a hat-trick from Valverde saw Madrid to take a 3–0 victory in the first leg of round of 16.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Champions League: Federico Valverde hat-trick punishes Man City with Real Madrid in control|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwy6w05gzwwt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=11 March 2026|access-date=12 March 2026|archive-date=12 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260312103226/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cwy6w05gzwwt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid got a 4–1 win against Elche, as [[Antonio Rüdiger]], Valverde, Huijsen and Güler got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Elche: Valverde scores again as Real Madrid cut gap on Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c8jx2w8n2vkt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 March 2026|access-date=14 March 2026|archive-date=14 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260314222105/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c8jx2w8n2vkt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 March, Madrid booked their place in the Champions League quarter-finals with a 2–1 win at Manchester City and 5–1 on aggregate, as Vinícius scored both goals for the team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hafez|first=Shamoon|title=Man City 1–2 Real Madrid (agg: 1–5) - Vinícius Jr and Haaland score|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjen8wk2ev5t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 March 2026|access-date=17 March 2026|archive-date=17 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317224328/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjen8wk2ev5t|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, another brace from Vinícius and Valverde's goal led Real to a 3–2 Madrid derby win over Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sutcliffe|first=Steven|title=Real Madrid 3–2 Atlético Madrid: Vinícius Júnior scores twice as Real narrow gap on Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjwzw41x3dwt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=22 March 2026|access-date=22 March 2026|archive-date=22 March 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260322223013/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjwzw41x3dwt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===April===
On 4 April, Madrid were beaten by Mallorca 1–2 on the road, with Militão scoring the only goal for Real.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Mallorca 2–1 Real Madrid: Vedat Muriqi stuns Real with late winner in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj0vz3jeqd3t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 April 2026|access-date=5 April 2026|archive-date=4 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260404203413/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj0vz3jeqd3t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid suffered a narrow 1–2 defeat at home against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final, as only Mbappé got on the scoresheet at the Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Real Madrid 1–2 Bayern Munich: Harry Kane and Luis Díaz give Bayern deserved edge|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9d4g9g3vzyt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=7 April 2026|access-date=9 April 2026|archive-date=9 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260409183904/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9d4g9g3vzyt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 April, Madrid were unable to get a win for the third match in a row, as they were held to a 1–1 draw against Girona with a goal from Valverde.<ref>{{cite web|last=Anderson|first=Jess|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Girona: Los Blancos continue stuttering form with home draw in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgrlqgzr0elt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=10 April 2026|access-date=11 April 2026|archive-date=11 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260411021251/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgrlqgzr0elt|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Madrid's Champions League campaign ended in a dramatic exit, as despite Güler's double and a goal from Mbappé, Real lost 3–4 at [[Allianz Arena]] and 4–6 on aggregate against the quarter-final's return leg opponents Bayern Munich.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bayern Munich 4–3 Real Madrid (6–4 on agg): German champions score two late goals to squeeze into Champions League semi-finals|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce84ryj43dmt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=15 April 2026|access-date=15 April 2026|archive-date=15 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260415214847/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce84ryj43dmt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 21 April, Madrid secured their first win in the last five matches, as goals from Mbappé and Vinícius gave Real a 2–1 victory over Alavés.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Alavés: Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior score to cut Barcelona's La Liga lead|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c87wqqj85wet|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=21 April 2026|access-date=22 April 2026|archive-date=22 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260422190044/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c87wqqj85wet|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid dropped points in the league once again, as they were held to a 1–1 draw at Real Betis with a goal from Vinícius.<ref>{{cite web|last=Anderson|first=Jess|title=Real Betis 1–1 Real Madrid: Title hopes fading for Los Blancos with La Liga draw|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn53nq6e2lqt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=24 April 2026|access-date=25 April 2026|archive-date=25 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260425080924/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn53nq6e2lqt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===May===
On 3 May, Madrid got a 2–0 win over Espanyol, thanks to a brace from Vinícius.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Espanyol 0-2 Real Madrid: Vinicius Junior double makes Barca wait for title|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy42y2dpk3yt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=3 May 2026|access-date=10 May 2026|archive-date=4 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260504045157/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy42y2dpk3yt|url-status=live}}</ref> Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde were involved in an altercation during training on 7 May that resulted in Valverde being knocked unconscious. Both players were fined €500,000 by the club.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Corrigan|first1=Dermot|last2=Cortegana|first2=Mario|last3=Rai|first3=Guillermo|title=Inside Real Madrid's dramatic descent into violence and chaos before El Clasico|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7262934/2026/05/08/real-madrid-tchouameni-valverde-clasico-arbeloa-perez/|work=The Athletic|date=8 May 2026|access-date=8 May 2026|url-access=limited|archive-date=8 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508121309/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7262934/2026/05/08/real-madrid-tchouameni-valverde-clasico-arbeloa-perez/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 May, Madrid suffered a 0–2 defeat against Barcelona in El Clásico at the [[Camp Nou|Spotify Camp Nou]]. The loss confirmed Barcelona as La Liga champions and condemned Madrid to a trophyless season for the first time since the [[2020–21 Real Madrid CF season|2020–21 campaign]].<ref>{{cite web|last=McKenna|first=Chris|title=Barcelona 2–0 Real Madrid: Marcus Rashford scores in El Clásico win as Barca win the title|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78qwgnn3vgt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=10 May 2026|access-date=22 May 2026|archive-date=11 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260511194108/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78qwgnn3vgt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid got a 2–0 home victory over Oviedo, courtesy of goals from Gonzalo García and Bellingham.<ref>{{cite web|last=Short|first=Michael|title=Kylian Mbappé jeered on Real Madrid return|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn4pgxz173pt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 May 2026|access-date=22 May 2026|archive-date=16 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516134143/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn4pgxz173pt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 May, a loan goal from Vinícius sealed a 1–0 win at Sevilla for Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|last=Keifer|first=MacDonald|title=Sevilla 0–1 Real Madrid: Vinícius Júnior scores only goal for visitors in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crrpqy7n475t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2026|access-date=22 May 2026|archive-date=18 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260518062342/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crrpqy7n475t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 May, Madrid concluded the season with a 4–2 home victory over Athletic Bilbao, with goals from Gonzalo García, Bellingham, Mbappé and Brahim. This game also marked the last appearance for [[Dani Carvajal]] and [[David Alaba]] with the club.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–2 Athletic Bilbao|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/athletic-club-vs-real-madrid/4NUvHRRRn2JYlWXx/|publisher=The Athletic|date=23 May 2026|access-date=25 May 2026<!--|archive-date=25 May 2026|archive-url=|url-status=live-->}}</ref>
